verdict.rationale: Composio's own Triggers feature detects events in connected apps, such as a new Slack message, GitHub commit or incoming email. It delivers each event as a signed structured payload to a registered webhook URL, which covers the event-detection half of the story natively. The evidence does not show a way to define rules inside Composio that run actions automatically; the consuming app must receive the webhook and decide what to do. missing for 10: built-in rule/condition definition, automatic event-to-action execution without user code, filtering or scheduling of trigger rules, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: When something happens in a connected app (a new Slack message, a GitHub commit, an incoming email), a trigger sends that event to your app as a structured payload.
You register it once per project, and Composio `POST`s every trigger event there, signed so you can verify it.
